comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C50-C51 regarding perturbation predictions. Both evaluations support these predictions as logical consequences of the model, though OpenEval rates them as UNCERTAIN (requiring experimental validation) while peer reviewers accept them as SUPPORTED testable hypotheses without challenge.

Strong agreement on claims C26-C28 regarding the extended Bayesian framework. Both evaluations support the theoretical foundation and integration of efficient coding with attractor dynamics. Peer review explicitly praises this integration as a 'beautiful achievement.'

Strong agreement on claims C42-C44, C47 comparing one-module vs two-module networks. Both evaluations support the finding that two-module networks are superior and more robust. OpenEval also includes C45, C48 which peer review addresses separately in R1.

Partial overlap on core architecture claims C3-C4. OpenEval R5 covers broader architecture details (C3-C7, C30-C33), while peer R1 focuses on the two-module superiority finding (C3-C4, C29, C34-C38, C45, C48). Both strongly support the two-module architecture as necessary and effective.

Overlap on network simulation results C34-C38. OpenEval R6 focuses on simulation methodology and low-dimensional analysis, while peer R1 emphasizes the overall success of the two-module model in capturing behavioral effects. Both evaluations are supportive.

Agreement on sensory module architecture claims C5, C30-C33. Both evaluations support the biological plausibility of the sensory module design and its consistency with neurophysiological data. Peer review also includes inhibitory learning claims C40-C41, C53.

Overlap on inhibitory modulation claims C40-C41. OpenEval R7 covers broader parameter exploration (C39-C41) while peer R2 focuses on biological plausibility of inhibitory mechanisms. Both support the critical role of inhibitory heterogeneity.

Agreement on claim C39 regarding inhibitory plasticity. Both evaluations accept this as established knowledge supported by appropriate citations. Peer review highlights this as an 'interesting prediction.'

Agreement on attractor model analysis claims C21-C23. Both evaluations support the systematic analysis of different attractor classes. Peer review also includes memory module characterization C6-C7 and accepts the coupled network dynamics.
Agreement on low-dimensional analysis claims C24-C25. Both evaluations support this analytical approach. Peer review treats it as a strength that provides intuition for network behavior.

Strong agreement on background/motivation claims C1-C2, C13-C16. OpenEval R1 also includes C14-C16 on model limitations. Both evaluations treat these as established background knowledge that motivates the study.

Agreement on theoretical background claims C8-C12. Both evaluations accept these as established prior work that provides essential context. Peer R6 covers broader background including empirical patterns C1-C2, C13-C20.
Agreement on empirical patterns claims C17-C20. Both evaluations support these as well-established experimental findings. Peer R6 treats these as accepted motivation for the modeling work.

Strong agreement on discussion/context claims C55-C60, C63-C64. Both evaluations support these as appropriate literature context and acknowledged limitations. OpenEval R15 covers broader discussion (C55-C67), while peer R10 also includes methodological details C54, C61-C62.

Agreement on acknowledged limitations claims C61-C62. Both evaluations support these as honest assessments of model boundaries. Peer review treats these as appropriately acknowledged future directions.

Agreement on broader implications claims C68-C70. Both evaluations support these contextual claims. OpenEval also includes C46 (experimental connections). Peer review accepts the speculation about modularity and repurposing as reasonable extrapolation.
Overlap on claim C46 regarding experimental connections. Both evaluations support the relationship to neurophysiological observations. Peer R9 also covers acknowledged limitations C49, C52.
Agreement on limitation claim C52 regarding distractors. Both evaluations support this as an appropriately acknowledged boundary of model scope.
Overlap on claim C53 regarding mechanistic insights and biological plausibility. Both evaluations support the connection to neurophysiological studies and accept the decoder method justification.
Overlap on claim C54 regarding methodological details. Both evaluations support these as appropriate discussion points with proper citations.
Agreement on broader context claims C65-C67. Both evaluations support these as appropriate positioning within the literature and reasonable implications for understanding working memory architecture.

Minor overlap on claims C45, C48 regarding mechanistic explanations for two-module superiority. OpenEval R8 focuses on comparative analysis, while peer R1 emphasizes overall model success. Both are supportive.

Minor overlap on memory module claims C6-C7. OpenEval R5 covers broader architecture including sensory module, while peer R3 focuses on attractor dynamics characterization. Both support the memory module design.

Minor overlap on claim C29 regarding iterative sensory-memory interaction. OpenEval R4 focuses on Bayesian framework extension, while peer R1 emphasizes overall two-module model success. Both are supportive.
